root.label: Smart pointers
root.note: unique_ptr owns alone, shared_ptr counts owners in a control block, weak_ptr observes.

children.label: unique_ptr
children.note: Move-only single owner; the deleter is part of the type.

children.label: Moved-from is null
children.note: The standard guarantees a moved-from unique_ptr holds nullptr.

children.label: Deleter size
children.note: Empty deleters cost nothing in practice; a function pointer deleter is stored. No size is guaranteed.

children.label: unique_ptr<T[]>
children.note: Calls delete[], offers operator[], and rejects derived-to-base conversions.

children.label: Pimpl destructor
children.note: Declare ~Widget in the header and define it where Impl is complete.

children.label: shared_ptr
children.note: An object pointer plus a control block pointer; the two need not agree.

children.label: Control block
children.note: Holds strong count, weak count, deleter and allocator.

children.label: Deleter from ctor type
children.note: shared_ptr<Base>(new Derived) deletes a Derived*, even without a virtual destructor.

children.label: make_shared
children.note: One allocation; the object's memory stays until the last weak_ptr is gone.

children.label: Aliasing constructor
children.note: Shares one object's ownership while pointing at another, such as a member.

children.label: Thread safety
children.note: Only the reference counts are synchronized.

children.label: Distinct copies
children.note: Different shared_ptr objects sharing a block may be used concurrently.

children.label: One shared object
children.note: Reading and assigning the same shared_ptr from two threads is a data race.

children.label: atomic<shared_ptr> (C++20)
children.note: Replaces the deprecated atomic_load free functions, removed in C++26.

children.label: weak_ptr
children.note: Points at the control block without keeping the object alive.

children.label: Breaking cycles
children.note: Make back edges weak so strong counts can reach zero.

children.label: lock()
children.note: Atomically yields an owner or an empty shared_ptr; expired() is only a hint.

children.label: shared_from_this
children.note: Needs an existing owner; throws bad_weak_ptr since C++17, UB before.

children.label: weak_from_this (C++17)
children.note: Returns an empty weak_ptr instead of throwing when unowned.

children.label: Interfaces
children.note: The parameter type states what happens to ownership.

children.label: T& or T*
children.note: Use without ownership; prefer these when the callee only reads or writes the object.

children.label: unique_ptr by value
children.note: A sink: the callee takes ownership and the caller must move.

children.label: out_ptr (C++23)
children.note: Resets at construction, stores the T** result at the end of the full-expression.

children.label: inout_ptr (C++23)
children.note: Releases the old pointer into the call; not usable with shared_ptr.

children.label: Double ownership
children.note: Two owners that do not know about each other delete twice.

children.label: Two from one raw
children.note: Each shared_ptr built from the same raw pointer makes its own control block.

children.label: shared_ptr(this)
children.note: Creates a second control block; use enable_shared_from_this.

children.label: Wrapping get()
children.note: A new owner of p.get() deletes what p will delete again.
